rationale: A wins because it turns the same facts into real, separate newsroom doors without pretending the announcement says more than it says. "Can you trust shopping advice from an AI that gets paid when you buy?" is a clean, grounded tension. B keeps reaching for drama the update does not earn, especially "Putting AI Search Directly Against Google Shopping and Amazon." That is how decent angles walk themselves into a fact-checking rake.
gaps_in_A: "after months of legal threats" adds a timeline the update never gives. Small wound, but still invented connective tissue.
"This angle is only pitchable by Perplexity itself as a transparency move" is too absolute. An accountability reporter could still own that story if Perplexity refuses to engage.
A uses "hundreds of millions of queries a month" as support but only really interrogates the self-reported nature in the refused angles. That skepticism belongs in the proof needs too.
gaps_in_B: "Putting AI Search Directly Against Google Shopping and Amazon" drags in competitors not in the update and turns a commerce feature into a platform fight the facts do not support.
"for the first time, an AI search product is inserting itself into the transaction" is an invented first-mover claim. Dangerous phrase, no proof.
"publishers and their legal teams will need to respond publicly" overstates the situation. No fact says threatened publishers are enrolled, eligible, contacted, or obliged to respond.
"publisher participation appears opt-in; content is cited regardless" is doing factual work the update does not support. If you have to write "appears," you do not have the fact.
